title: World Games
build: Epyx disk, 1986, two sides (C64 Preservation Project G64s, world_games_s1[epyx_1986](pal) and world_games_s2[epyx_1986](pal), MD5 2ab5a751... and f983b43d...)

$0F3D = $0C, which nothing reads; no log frame drawn yet ($0F3B = $FF), lumberjack 1's picture $0A; the standing lumberjacks' pictures unpacked ($2992, with $0F42 = 0)

the balance meters in screen row 22: lumberjack 2's at columns 2-9 and 11-18, lumberjack 1's at 21-28 and 30-37. From the middle out, one character for every three of lean, $73 filled and $0E empty: to the left for a lean below 0, to the right above

lumberjack 1 leaning the other way

draws the log in frame A, 0 to 3, from its list ($1D91) into the screen from ($D7): runs of characters, each ended by $FF and then how far on from its start the next run begins ($24, $28 or $2C: a row down, and four columns left, none or four right); a second $FF ends the list

picks each lumberjack's picture for the frame. Lumberjack 1: a new arm pose asked for ($0F5E, from $2107) becomes its pose ($0F62); when it leans 24 or more and no less than the other, pose 11, the teeter; the picture from $1FD2
a new picture: kept in $0C and the sprites rebuilt ($D9 = 0); for the teeter, its sound (tune 5) with its slide step from $1FF4; for poses 2 and 5, a foot landing on the log (tune 3)
lumberjack 2, the same from $0F5F, $0F63 and $1FE3, its picture into $0D: the teeter when it leans further than lumberjack 1 and by 24 or more

lumberjack 2's teeter: its step goes to $3723, track 5's, but it starts tune 5, lumberjack 1's, where tune 6 was meant: the pulse-wave teeter on voice 3 is never heard, and lumberjack 2 teeters with lumberjack 1's sawtooth and step
both pictures picked
lumberjack 1's picture for each pose: the run, poses 0 to 5, then the arms flung out from 6, 9, 13 or 15 to 16, with 11 the teeter
lumberjack 2's pictures, laid out the same

the teeter sound's slide step by the lean less 16. Only a lean of 24 or more teeters, so the first eight are never read and every lean up to 31 gives $F8; a lean of 32 or 33 reads the two $EA after, and a larger one the code at $2006

the game's work each frame, from the interrupt: nothing while the fall's pictures unpack ($0F49 = 1); straight after (2), the fall's start ($2B97); after a fall, its pictures ($2C22); at a bout's end ($0F41 negative), the next ($31D5)

the fall test: a lumberjack whose lean ($0F70, $0F71) has reached 24 either way falls; when both have, the one leaning further, or lumberjack 1 when they are level. The other's lean is set to 0, $0F41 = 1, the sprite list held ($D9 = 1), the shapes on screen copied out of the unpacker's way ($2CE9), and the fall's pictures chosen ($0F42): $18 when lumberjack 1 fell, $0C for lumberjack 2
the fall's pictures unpacked: on to the fall itself

no fall: for each lumberjack the stick ($20C6) and the lean ($2297); the log's speed ($2234) and its turn ($22C9); the sounds and the pictures ($1C56); each one's feet slowing ($21D2); and the rumble ended (tune 8) while the log turns at less than 2

a lumberjack's stick, X 0 or 1. Its wobble ($0F66) dies down by one a frame, except while it stands quite still, its feet at rest, on a turning log: then it only grows ($22EA). Then the stick ($2DB3): the fire button, as it goes down, turns the lumberjack round to run the other way ($0F68) and hands its push to the log ($2209)
left or right: pushed while leaning 16 or more, the arms flung out ($0F5E): pose 6, or 15 when the feet run backwards, for right; 9 or 13 for left

a change between left, right and both is a step: the push handed to the log ($2209), the feet faster by 7 the way the lumberjack runs ($2183), and pose 5 or 2 the one to settle in ($0F64); the stick held as it was, the push grows by one a frame ($CB + X), up to 255
the stick done

a step: the feet's speed ($0F6A low, $0F6C high) up by 7 the way the lumberjack runs ($0F68). Running forwards it is held at 127; running backwards, a step taken at -122 or below wraps round, and the speed is set to $FFFF, -1/256: the feet all but stop
running backwards: 7 taken off
the feet's speed falls toward 0 by $50/256 a frame
a step or a turn hands the lumberjack's push to the log: an eighth of the frames the stick was held ($CB + X), signed by the way they run, added to the log's spin ($0F5D), held to 31 either way

every 16th frame the log's spin ($0F5D) loses one toward 0 ($23D2); then the log's speed ($0F3A) is its spin plus both lumberjacks' push so far, an eighth of $CB and of $CC, each signed by the way its lumberjack runs, held to 31 either way
a lumberjack's lean ($0F70 + X): a quarter of its feet's speed less the log's speed, with four times its wobble ($0F66) added the way it already leans

the log's turn: it moves on a frame ($0F3C, 0 to 3, one way or the other by the sign of its speed) every so many frames by its speed, one more than $23F2 gives: 12 at speed 1 down to 2 at 31, or at once when it has sped up past the wait. Each step adds one to both lumberjacks' wobble

lumberjack 1's legs: when its feet run at 32 or more, the pose ($0F62) steps on every so many frames by a quarter of their speed ($23F2), forward or back the way they run, 0 to 5 and round (or, from an arm pose, on to 16 and back to 0); slower, the pose steps every 12 frames until it reaches the one to settle in ($0F64)
lumberjack 2's legs, the same with $0F63, $0F65, $0F69, $0F6D and $0F73
the legs done
the change to the spin's size, by its size: 0 at 0, otherwise -1
the waits between the log's steps, and the legs', by speed 0 to 31: 11 at 1 down to 1 at 31, each a frame short of the steps' spacing
bytes nothing reads: waits for speeds past 31, which never come

builds the frame's list of sprites from both lumberjacks' pictures. Each picture n has a record ($8000 + 2n): its number of sprites, then four bytes for each, x, y and the shape's address; $8100 + 2n moves it from the lumberjack's place ($0E-$10, $11-$13). Each sprite's x ($73 + n, the ninth bit in $B3, $B4), y ($82 + n), shape number ($91 + n) and the shape's last byte ($A0 + n): its colour, and bits for multicolour ($B1, $B2), double width ($B5, $B6) and double height ($B7, $B8). At most 15
lumberjack 2's sprites after lumberjack 1's

eight zeros, then the bits again for sprites 8 to 15, in the second byte of each pair

sorts the sprites by height: each one's rank ($64 + n) is how many sit above it. By rank, the first eight go to set 0 ($28 x, $37 y, $46 shape, $55 colour; their bits in $1C, $18, $20 and $24) and the rest after them ($30, $3F, $4E, $5D; their bits in $1F, $1B, $23, $27)

splits the sprites past the eighth into up to three bands. With eight or fewer there are none: the bands' lines are left at $D4, $D7 and $DA and reload nothing. Otherwise a band starts at the next sprite still to show and reloads as many hardware sprites, counted from the top, as have finished by then, 21 lines each ($C5 and $C8 for the first, $C6 and $C9 the second, $C7 and $CA the third); with six or more free the first does it all
each band's line set 2 above, and each count held to the number of sprites past eight

the sprites to switch on among the first eight, by the number of sprites: 0, 1, 3 … $FF from eight on
the sprites past the eighth to switch on, by the number of sprites: none up to eight, then 1, 3 … $7F

a lumberjack's stick, X 0 or 1, as $DC00 reads it, bits low when pressed. Before the bout starts, the join screen instead ($2F0E). The computer's lumberjack (its port, $0F75 + X, equal to $0F02) gets its move from $2DC9; the others read their port, $DC00 + $0F75,X

the computer's move. With any wobble, it holds ($2E41). Otherwise from its lean without the wobble (its feet's speed over 4 less the log's speed): when that has the sign of the way it runs, fire ($EF), which turns it round; when it has the log's sign, nothing ($FF); otherwise its style for that lean ($2E98): 0 holds, 1 steps when the log turns at 24 or more or it stepped less than four frames ago, and holds otherwise
fire: turns the computer round
its style for this lean
a step: the stick to the other side, left after right and right otherwise
held: right after right, otherwise left
the move in A, and Y back
picks the computer's style for the bout: one of the 16 patterns at $2EB8, at random, its 16 bits into $2E98-$2EA7, a byte each

the 16 styles, two bytes each, the highest bit first for leans 0 to 15: $FFFF steps at every lean, $E000 only at the smallest
the styles' second bytes, the bits for leans 8 to 15, as $2E72 reads them

the generator's working byte, stored here by $2EF2

against the computer, the player's fire: on port 1 the player is lumberjack 2 on port 1 and the computer lumberjack 1 ($0F02 = $0F75 = 0); on port 2 the player takes port 2 and the computer port 1's place ($0F02 = $0F75 = 1); then the names ($326C), and $0F74 = $FF
two players: the first one's name, "PRESS YOUR BUTTON" and the try
the first player's fire: on port 1 they are lumberjack 2 on port 1 ($0F76 = 1), the second player lumberjack 1 on port 2; on port 2 the other way round. $0F74 = 2
no move this frame

draws who meets whom: two bytes a pair from $0F06, 9 for the computer, $0F05 the bytes in use. With one joystick for all ($087D = 1) each player meets the computer in turn; one player meets the computer; otherwise the players are paired at random, the computer taking the place of an odd one out at random. Three tries ($0F17 = 2)
one joystick: each player against the computer
players paired at random

a bout's end: the computer's mark cleared ($0F02); while pairs remain, the screen off and the next bout ($1053). After the last pair: in practice ($081D bit 7) "TRY AGAIN? Y" ($3205); otherwise the next try from the first pair, and after the third, back to the shell ($0F77 = $FF)

practice's end: "TRY AGAIN? Y" in the text row once, the answer moved by the stick (up Y, down N, at $77E3; $0F51) and taken with fire: yes plays again from the first pair, no ends the event ($0F77 = $FF)
the event over: $0F77 = $FF, which the interrupt at line $FB takes back to the shell
no fire: up for Y, down for N

the text row for a bout: cleared to character 0 in white; the pair's first player's record, 16 characters (the name and the country), on the left, the second's at column 24 or "COMPUTER"; the clock, "0:00:0" in green, between; the clock reset
16 characters of the player's record ($0800 + X) to ($08)
"COMPUTER" for the computer's side
the player in pair slot X ($0F06 + X) into $0F16, and 32 times it in X, where their record is in page $08
"COMPUTER" and eight spaces
the clock's start, "0:00:0"
"TRY AGAIN? Y"

the clock, from the interrupt at line $DD, while the bout runs: the hundredths ($0F4E) go up by 1 and 2 on alternate frames, and at 98 or more the seconds ($0F50) go on, so a second on the clock lasts about 65 frames; at 60 seconds the minutes ($0F4F).
